articles.title: HMRC increases scrutiny of residential valuations
articles.summary: HMRC is increasingly challenging residential property valuations in inheritance tax (IHT) returns, with the number of cases referred to the Valuation Office Agency (VOA) rising 23.5% in the last year, according to research from TWM Solicitors, a private wealth and family law firm.
articles.ai_summary:
- HMRC is ramping up scrutiny of residential property valuations for inheritance tax, leading to a 23.5% increase in cases referred to the Valuation Office Agency.  
- TWM Solicitors' research highlights significant growing enforcement against potentially undervalued property declarations in IHT returns.

articles.title: Four in five landlords unprepared for Renters’ Right Act
articles.summary: Four in five landlords (82%) are concerned about the impact of the Renters’ Rights Act, with one in two (44%) very concerned. Meanwhile, three-quarters (75%) of landlords say regulation has made them less likely to grow their portfolios, and half (49%) are planning to sell or reduce their stake within two months.
articles.ai_summary:
- **Landlord Alarm:** 82% of landlords express concern over the upcoming Renters’ Rights Act, with 44% feeling very anxious about its implications.  
- **Portfolio Retreat:** 75% of landlords are deterred from expanding their portfolios, with nearly half (49%) considering selling or reducing their investments within two months.

articles.ai_summary:
- Landlords face mounting pressure to enhance EPC ratings to attract tenants, with a new requirement to reach a minimum "C" rating by 2030 looming.
